x: Jack Frost gained a "double" in the sprints. Tom Wiley, who has been unable to compete much this season, showed us that he is still fit by gaining us valuable points in the Field Events, and helping us to win the Relay.
In the sprint, after several false starts, Liffen just beat Jack Frost, but Jack reversed the positions in the furlong by about a yard and a half.
Jack Frost too, had had a strenuous Saturday, having won the furlong for the A.A.A. at Oxford, was unplaced in his heat in the 100 yards, and gave the furlong a miss.

As it was a close match resulted, and grand performances were put up by our sprinters, Jack Frost and Fred Clay, against such opposition, with Jack Brown, our A.A.A. junior 880 yards champion, others giving their usual sterling performances.

We are glad to say that many of them will be able to turn out for us, duties permitting. One case in point is our Track Captain, Jack Frost, now with the R.A.F. Jack is stationed near London, and hopes to turn up regularly.

Jack Frost is now in the R.A.F. and has been stationed in Norfolk, but hopes to turn out for us during the coming Track Season. If Jack can reach the form which he showed when he won the Club 300 yards' Handicap from scratch last September in 33.8 secs., he will take some beating.

Young Briggs has shown good form in the Junior events in which he has competed and Jack Frost has taken to running 440 yards hurdles. He might well prove an excellent performer if he will concentrate on improving his style over the obstacles.
Among the sprinters, Teddy Read improved by leaps and bounds as the season progressed, and was given good support by Dicky Dumbrill and Jack Frost.
Len Marchant was behind Parlett of Dorking over the half-mile stage, but Jack Frost pulled up a little, and then Dicky Dumbrill almost caught his man over the first 220.

Pauls, and Jack Frost ran a fine third leg to make up lost ground. On the same evening the 3 Miles Team Race was decided, but owing to unforeseen circumstances, we only had three distance men available, but A.
Wickerson, the well-known sprinter, who was running for Cambridge. Jack Frost, our track Vice-Captain, was second, and Dicky Dumbrill fourth. The 220 Yards saw Jack Frost an easy winner and A.
McDonald Bailey, the West Indian runner, won the 100 Yards for the Poly, and Jack Frost ran well to gain third place for us. Dicky Dumbrill also ran third in the second race over this distance.

Jack Frost ran second in the 100 Yards, and also finished third in the 220, which was won by Teddy Read. Syd Jarlett and Bob Wise finished second and third in the 440, and Len Marchant won the 880 Yards, with Alf Orton fourth.
Jack Frost won the 100 Yards, although the judges thought differently, and he also captured the 220. Bob Wise finished second in the 440, and V.
Jack Frost beat Reynolds of the Police in the 100 Yards with Stan Botwright third. The latter, however, won the 220 with Ted Read in second place.

Jack Frost also beat Morris in the 440, with Bob Wise in third place. Blowfield and Jimmy Wood had no real opposition in the Mile while Bill Lucas and Charlie Smart also ran home together in the 2 Miles event.
The 100 Yards Club Championship was won by Ted Read, who beat Dicky Dumbrill with Jack Frost third, and the holder, Stan Botwright, beaten into fourth place.
Higgins, the Public Schools' quarter champion, beat Ted Read in the 220, and scored a double by also winning the 440, in which Jack Frost finished third.
With three heats in the 300 Yards, the following qualified : Jack Frost, off the scratch mark, Bob Wise, P.

In the 4 x 100 Yards Relay our four ran second to Achilles, our runners were Teddy Read, Dicky Dumbrill, Jack Frost and Michael Broadbent. Another Relay success was at Guildford, Lulham, Hawkins, Osmint and Read each pulled away from their rivals.

Harley (Senior), Etienne Gailly, George Durrant, Derrick Burfitt, Norman Graves and the Wirral A.C. (with a Wirral whisper!), Dick Towndrow, Mr. and Mrs. Jack Frost, Oscar Horwood, Alan, Eric and Leonard Bishop, Mr. and Mrs.
Cope and Jack Frost, the holder, had a neck-and-neck struggle with Cope getting the verdict. Paxton finished third and this lad should show great improvement next season.

It was a neck-and-neck struggle between South London Harriers and ourselves throughout, and our members can be said to have done well against such opposition. Ted Read ran second to Liffen of S.L.H. in the 100, while Jack Frost was second in the first strings 220 yards, and E.
For the 440 yards we had Jack Frost and Jim Beaumont taking first two places, while Bill Lucas won the 1 mile in 4 min. 34.3 secs., with Frank Abberton in third place.
I remember Jack Frost - a sprinter during World War II and Albert Frost - a regular member of our cross-country and road relay teams just after the War.
